content:
library(munsell) 
library(colorspace) 
library(htmlwidgets)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(shiny)
library(dygraphs)
library(xts)

df <- read.csv('weekly_other_faq_tail_risk.csv')
ab_df <- read.csv('weekly_other_faq_tail_risk_garch_coefs.csv')


df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert the first column to Date
    across(2, as.Date), 
    # Convert all columns from the second one onwards to numeric (float)
    across(3:ncol(.), as.numeric)
  )

ab_df <- ab_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert the first column to Date
    across(2, as.Date), 
    # Convert all columns from the second one onwards to numeric (float)
    across(3:ncol(.), as.numeric)
  )
ab_df$a1_plus_b1 <- ab_df$alpha1 + ab_df$beta1
# ab_df$variance <- ab_df$omega/(1-ab_df$a1_plus_b1)

ab_df %>% filter(a1_plus_b1 >= 0.99)
# Prepare data for Dygraphs (requires XTS objects)
sensitivity_xts <- xts(cbind(ab_df$alpha1, ab_df$beta1, ab_df$a1_plus_b1),
                       order.by = ab_df$Date)
colnames(sensitivity_xts) <- c("alpha1", "beta1", "a1+b1")

skew_xts <- xts(cbind( ab_df$skew, ab_df$shape),
                order.by = ab_df$Date)
colnames(skew_xts) <- c('skew', 'shape')

# Graph 1: Price and Surge
price_xts <- xts(cbind(df$Actual_Price, df$Surge_Price),
                 order.by = df$Date)
colnames(price_xts) <- c("Price", "95_Surge_Limit")

# Graph 2: Returns and Risk
log_risk_xts <- xts(cbind(df$Actual_Return, df$VaR_Upper, df$CVaR_Upper),
                    order.by = df$Date)
risk_xts <- xts(cbind(df$Simple_Ret_Pct, df$Simple_VaR_Pct, df$Simple_CVaR_Pct),
                order.by = df$Date)

colnames(log_risk_xts) <- c("Return", "VaR_95", "CVaR")
colnames(risk_xts) <- c("Return", "VaR_95", "CVaR")

ui <- fluidPage(
  # Custom CSS for the 20% width vertical sidebar and sticky behavior
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      #explanation-column {
        height: 100vh;
        position: sticky;
        top: 0;
        background-color: #f4f7f6;
        border-right: 2px solid #bdc3c7;
        padding: 20px;
        overflow-y: auto;
      }
      .metric-title { font-weight: bold; color: #2c3e50; font-size: 1.4em; margin-bottom: 15px; border-bottom: 2px solid #e74c3c; padding-bottom: 5px; }
      .metric-desc { color: #34495e; line-height: 1.6; font-size: 1.1em; }
      .highlight-box { color: #7f8c8d; font-style: italic; margin-top: 20px; font-size: 0.9em; }
    "))
  ),
  
  titlePanel("Interactive Onion Risk Dashboard: Pune Market"),
  
  fluidRow(
    # Left Column: 20% Width (approx. 2 or 3 in Bootstrap 12-column grid)
    column(3, 
           div(id = "explanation-column",
               uiOutput("metricDescription")
           )
    ),
    
    # Right Column: 80% Width
    column(9,
           # Wrap each plot in a div to capture mouse hover
           div(onmouseover = "Shiny.setInputValue('hovered_plot', 'price')", 
               dygraphOutput("pricePlot", height = "180px")),
           br(),
           div(onmouseover = "Shiny.setInputValue('hovered_plot', 'logRisk')", 
               dygraphOutput("logRiskPlot", height = "180px")),
           br(),
           div(onmouseover = "Shiny.setInputValue('hovered_plot', 'risk')", 
               dygraphOutput("riskPlot", height = "180px")),
           br(),
           div(onmouseover = "Shiny.setInputValue('hovered_plot', 'sens')", 
               dygraphOutput("sensPlot", height = "180px")),
           br(),
           div(onmouseover = "Shiny.setInputValue('hovered_plot', 'skew')", 
               dygraphOutput("skewPlot", height = "180px"))
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$metricDescription <- renderUI({
    hover <- input$hovered_plot
    
    if (is.null(hover)) {
      return(tagList(
        div(class="metric-title", "Market Intelligence"),
        div(class="metric-desc", "Hover over any graph on the right to see the technical breakdown of Pune's Onion price risk metrics.")
      ))
    }
    
    # Define the content using lists for bullet points
    content <- switch(hover,
                      "price" = list(
                        title = "Price & Surge Limit",
                        points = list(
                          "Shows the actual market price vs. the 95% Surge Limit.",
                          "If the black line crosses the dashed red line, the market is in a 'statistical anomaly' zone where standard interventions usually fail."
                        )
                      ),
                      "logRisk" = list(
                        title = "Log Returns & Tail Risk",
                        points = list(
                          "Visualizes volatility via log-transformed returns.",
                          "Blue line (VaR): The minimum expected loss in a 'bad' week.",
                          "Orange line (CVaR): The 'Expected Shortfall'—the average magnitude of a crash if the VaR threshold is breached."
                        )
                      ),
                      "risk" = list(
                        title = "Realized Risk (%)",
                        points = list(
                          "Converts complex log-returns into simple percentage moves for easier policy intuition.",
                          "Use the bottom slider to isolate historic crises like the 2013 or 2019 price shocks."
                        )
                      ),
                      "sens" = list(
                        title = "GARCH Sensitivity",
                        points = list(
                          "Alpha1 (Purple): 'Nervousness'—how much today's shock dictates tomorrow's price.",
                          "Beta1 (Brown): 'Persistence'—how long a period of high volatility lasts.",
                          "Sum (Red): If Alpha1 + Beta1 is near 1.0, the market has 'infinite memory' of shocks and is highly unstable.",
                          "     High α1​ / Low β1​ - Hypersensitive - Flash-Crash prone -Violent, short-lived spikes.",
                          "     Low α1​ / High β1​ - Persistent Sticky Volatility Prices stay high/unstable for months.",
                          "     Sum > 1.0 - Non-Stationary - Explosive - The variance is technically infinite; the model is breaking.",
                          "     Sum < 0.90 - Stable - Mean-Reverting - Prices eventually settle back to normal levels."
                          
                          
                        )
                      ),
                      "skew" = list(
                        title = "Skew & Shape (Tail Risk)",
                        points = list(
                          "Skew: Values > 1 indicate the market is structurally biased toward upward price explosions rather than drops.",
                          "Shape (Cyan): Measures 'Black Swan' thickness. Values below 3.0 mean extreme, outlier events are now frequent and expected."
                        )
                      )
    )
    
    # Render the title and the unordered list
    tagList(
      div(class="metric-title", content$title),
      div(class="metric-desc", 
          tags$ul(
            lapply(content$points, tags$li)
          )
      ),
      div(class="highlight-box", "Data Source: OGD Maharashtra (2007-2025)")
    )
  })
  
  # --- Your Existing Dygraph Plotting Code ---
  output$pricePlot <- renderDygraph({
    dygraph(price_xts, group = "onion_sync") %>%
      dySeries("Price", color = "black") %>%
      dySeries("95_Surge_Limit", color = "red", strokePattern = "dashed") %>%
      dyAxis("y", label = "INR/kg")
  })
  
  # Plot 1
  output$pricePlot <- renderDygraph({
    dygraph(price_xts, group = "onion_sync") %>%
      dySeries("Price", color = "black") %>%
      dySeries("95_Surge_Limit", color = "red", strokePattern = "dashed") %>%
      dyAxis("y", label = "Price (INR/kg)")
  })
  
  # Plot 2
  output$logRiskPlot <- renderDygraph({
    dygraph(log_risk_xts, group = "onion_sync") %>%
      dySeries("Return", color = "rgba(150,150,150,0.5)") %>%
      dySeries("VaR_95", color = "blue") %>%
      dySeries("CVaR", color = "orange") %>%
      dyAxis("y", label = "Log Return")
  })
  
  # Plot 3
  output$riskPlot <- renderDygraph({
    dygraph(risk_xts, group = "onion_sync") %>%
      dySeries("Return", color = "rgba(150,150,150,0.5)") %>%
      dySeries("VaR_95", color = "blue") %>%
      dySeries("CVaR", color = "orange") %>%
      dyAxis("y", label = "Return") %>%
      dyRangeSelector(height = 20) # Adds the bottom slider
  })
  
  output$sensPlot <- renderDygraph({
    dygraph(sensitivity_xts, group = "onion_sync") %>%
      dySeries("alpha1", color = "purple") %>%
      dySeries("beta1", color = "#07e337") %>%
      dySeries("a1+b1", color = "red") %>%
      dyAxis("y", label = "Sensitivity")
  })
  
  output$skewPlot <- renderDygraph({
    dygraph(skew_xts, group = "onion_sync") %>%
      dySeries("skew", color = "black") %>%
      dySeries("shape", color = "cyan") %>%
      dyAxis("y", label = "Sensitivity")
  })
}


shinyApp(ui, server)
